answer: A river ferry license covers one crossing per applicant on one river stretch for 120 days. The keeper posts a 150 token deposit and a 90 dollar license before the first dawn run. Each crossing needs a numbered ticket, and the keeper logs time, passengers, and toll, signed by a neighbor. The whisper-quiet motor carries a serial number, checked on stubs. A forged tally forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 ferries freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A fake fleet is painted boats with no river under them, and an inspector asking for a stub sinks it.
